focus.label: Viral wart (HPV) post-laser
focus.why: CO2 laser disrupts epidermis, potentially activating or inoculating HPV; verrucoid papules are characteristic; no response to topical anti-inflammatory/antibiotic/eczema therapy supports viral etiology.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of post-laser HPV reactivation, the retrieved biopsies reveal verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and hypergranulotic keratinizing cells, supporting a neoplastic/precancerous keratosis rather than definitive viral wart. HPV PCR/genotyping was not obtained, so viral etiology cannot be fully excluded or confirmed. The verrucoid morphology and poor response to topical therapy align with actinic keratosis in this photodamaged patient with prior basal cell carcinoma. All available key histopathological information is covered, though molecular HPV testing remains missing.

payload.analysis: Two biopsies showing verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and no koilocytes, combined with photodamage and prior basal cell carcinoma, strongly support precancerous verrucous actinic keratosis and refute viral wart and benign keratotic papules; unresponsiveness to anti-inflammatory/antibiotic therapy argues against dermatitis. payload.report: The patient's verrucoid keratotic papules after laser resurfacing, on a background of photodamage and prior basal cell carcinoma, failed conservative therapy. Two biopsies showed verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and no koilocytes or viral cytopathic effect, strongly supporting a precancerous keratosis and excluding viral wart and benign keratotic papules. Lack of response to topical treatment argues against dermatitis. Although HPV PCR/genotyping was not performed, leaving minor uncertainty, the evidence strongly favors verrucous actinic keratosis, a specific precancerous lesion, refining the broader frontier of skin cancer or precancer.
